title: Accessory Drive Locations — 2.3L EcoBoost
introduction:
I start this 2.3L EcoBoost map at the crankshaft belt pulley, where engine rotation enters the external belt drive. From there, trace the blue paths in the illustration and match their callouts to the table. Keeping the engine identity beside the drawing matters: a familiar-looking pulley is a poor substitute for the correct layout.

The accessory drive includes a tensioner and a separately identified idler pulley assembly. Their jobs differ. The spring-loaded tensioner maintains belt tension; the idler guides the belt along its route. Think of the idler as a bend in the road and the tensioner as the part keeping the belt from arriving slack. The coolant pump and generator pulleys transfer belt motion to their respective accessories.

The A/C compressor belt is identified separately from the accessory belt, as is the compressor pulley. I trace that belt’s own path rather than assuming the accessory tensioner releases it. A pulley label identifies the belt-contact wheel, not every part of the assembly behind it.

Use this reference to recognize the components and their illustrated relationships. It does not establish removal access, tensioner-release direction, belt-installation steps or diagnostic limits. Continue with the matching service information before disturbing either belt. The external accessory drive is also distinct from the engine’s internal timing drive.
